events.note: Eight rivals face the jury they will create.

events.name: Ash
events.text: My objective is to win the best prize, and that means making strategic decisions from the start. I need to create a compelling but guarded reason for being here that will appeal to the future jury without revealing my true ruthless ambition.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need to establish a strong, calculating persona. I will signal ambition without overcommitting to alliances yet.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need appear motivated without revealing leverage or strategy.

events.name: Dara
events.text: No jury yet. I should sound self-interested but not cruel, so eliminated rivals might still rank me high later.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need to sound driven but not too emotional; the jury will judge. A terse, personal motive works.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need to establish myself as a formidable but not overtly threatening player. The jury will remember everything, so I should project confidence without painting a target on my back. I'll hint at strategic depth to attract potential allies while keeping my true intentions hidden.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Intro phase; I should sound guarded and purposeful without revealing much. Jury will judge me later, so keep the motive sharp but not warm.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Intro sets my public image for jury; claim personal stakes to build sympathy without allying yet.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm here to prove my strategic mind and secure a future I've only dreamed of, a future I will fight for.

events.name: Bex
events.text: The prize buys freedom. Every rival is an obstacle; the jury remembers who they let win.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I’m here to secure the best prize by outlasting everyone who underestimates how seriously I’m playing.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm here for the top prize: it buys my freedom, not anyone else's. Expect loyalty priced exactly at survival.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm here because this prize buys my family's freedom from a debt that's been crushing us.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I came to outthink, not outlast—precision over chaos, always.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I want the prize because I've spent years being overlooked, and I intend to finally be the one who wins.

events.name: Hana
events.text: The prize is my ticket out of debt, securing my family's future—no matter the cost.

events.name: Ash
events.text: My goal is to win the best prize, which means I need to be in the final three. Alliances can help me survive the early rounds, but I need to be careful not to form too many or trust the wrong people. Given the limited number of allies allowed in the final three, I should try to s

events.name: Bex
events.text: Pacts offer temporary safety and political leverage. Dara is a direct rival for the top prize but her 'loyalty priced at survival' suggests she values transactional alliances highly. A pact with her provides mutual protection without emotional baggage, which appeals to my desire

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara, we both want freedom. Let's lock arms this round; you save me, I save you.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need visible options without creating obligations. Offer to a useful, jury-sensitive rival while preserving flexibility.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Cole offers Hana a pact: mutual survival, no promises beyond that.

events.name: Dara
events.text: A pact buys safety early; I pick Ash, seems strategic and will trade honestly. Betrayal later remains possible.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash: pact on the wristband. Loyalty priced exactly at survival, as promised. I keep my bargains.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need allies but not trust; offer a pact to Bex, who seems pragmatic and might be useful.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex, I'm a pragmatist too. Temporary pact to navigate the early hazards?

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eight contestants, need to reach final three. Early pacts are risky—betrayals cost jury votes. Better to observe first round, then commit in round 2 when I know who's making moves. Dara's 'loyalty priced at survival' signals a potential calculator like me, but I won't tip my hand

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Watching the board before I move. Precision, not haste.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Early pact window; forming a pact with a strong but non-threatening rival can protect me. Eli's stated family debt suggests a motive that may make him loyal, so I'll offer him a pact.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Gus here. I'll offer a wristband pact to Eli. Let's keep each other alive through the hazards.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Pacts stage, early game. No one to target yet. Wait and observe offers first.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Dara offered me a pact, and it seems like a good deal for survival. I should accept it to ensure my safety this round.
I accept your pact. Let's survive this.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I must decide between Dara and Eli. Dara is the stronger ally for hazard survival, but Eli offers a pact now which guarantees an alliance. I will accept Eli's offer to secure an immediate partner and avoid being isolated if Dara hesitates or breaks.
I'll take your hand. Don't let me drown.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Hana has my outstanding offer but no acceptance. I should expand options without creating obligations yet.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I’m keeping options open; no pact is real until both sides accept.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Accepting Bex gives me a mutual-save ally while my Ash offer stays open. Two partners, no debts yet.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Bex, accepted. Mutual survival, priced exactly. Ash, my offer stands.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus offered me a pact; accepting gives me cover without binding me to Bex's offer. I will accept Gus only.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: No one offered me a pact in round 1, so I have no accept option. I need to secure a partner now or enter hazards alone. Gus offered Eli, Eli offered Bex, Bex offered Dara, Dara offered Ash, Cole offered Hana. That leaves me and possibly Hana as outsiders. Hana hasn't accepted Col

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana. No one else reached for you. I will.
Cole's offer is thin. Mine has teeth.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eli has offered me nothing yet but I offered Eli a pact; Eli's offer to Bex and mine to Eli are open. Accepting requires an offer to me, which doesn't exist, so I can only offer again or wait. Waiting keeps my options open without giving free loyalty.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole offered me a pact; accepting gives mutual protection now, can betray later if needed. No one else offering to me. Better than waiting.

events.note: Elect a Guide to call the safe path.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need to become the Guide to gain an advantage and control the path. Campaigning is the only way to achieve this.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I will campaign to be the Guide. My strategic mind will ensure our survival.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Bex wants to win. If she is the Guide, she can ensure her survival and control who else survives. She must campaign hard.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I know the path. Vote Bex as Guide; I guarantee safety for three.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Being Guide guarantees survival and offers decisive leverage, but public trust is limited. Campaign aggressively while preserving Hana’s pact.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Vote Cole as Guide. I can carry the bridge, and everyone sees whether my calls hold.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Being Guide guarantees survival but invites betrayal suspicion. Better to back a puppet Guide while keeping my pacts intact. Cole looks controllable.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'll back a Guide who commits to honest calls. Cole, want my vote? My pacts stay solid.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need to push for Guide to control survival, but Bex trusts me. Breaking Bex now might earn jury hate; Gus pact is useful too. Campaign to win the vote.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I know the bridge. Trust me, I'll keep us alive.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm isolated: no pacts. Cole offered me one but I didn't accept. Hana hasn't accepted mine yet. The Bex-Eli-Gus and Ash-Dara-Bex blocs have numbers. If I campaign for Guide, I need votes from somewhere. Better to let someone else win Guide, survive the bridge, and position for th

events.name: Gus
events.text: I hold a pact with Eli, but Eli and Bex are paired too, so the pact web is tangled. Campaigning for Guide lets me control the safe path and gain leverage; breaking my pact now gains nothing yet.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'll be your Guide. Trust the path I call, or lose your footing and your life.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole pact is set but noncommittal from him. Fenn offers alternative alliance privately. Campaign for Guide control now.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'll lead us safely across. Elect me Guide.
Your offer intrigues. Respond after votes?

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need to vote for a Guide. My campaign is over, and I need to secure my position. Cole seems like a strong candidate, and he has a pact with Hana. Bex is also campaigning strongly. I'll vote for Cole; it might align me with Hana later.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I vote for Cole to be our Guide. He has proven his strength.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need votes to become Guide and control the bridge. Ash is a rival with Dara, so I will offer Gus my vote if he supports me, hoping to secure a majority.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus, back Bex as Guide and I’ll ensure you cross safely. We can control this together.
Vote Bex. I'll call your path true. Trust me.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need the Guide role to control survival and gain leverage. My existing pact with Hana provides one vote, while Dara’s public offer may be useful but unreliable.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Vote Cole. I know my calls will be tested publicly, and survival makes betrayal costly.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Two pacts with Ash and Bex; Bex claims path knowledge. Voting Bex builds goodwill with two jury-relevant allies without lying myself.
My vote is yours. Guide me honestly or that pact dies.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I should vote for myself to try to become Guide and gain control; my pact with Gus doesn't require otherwise.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Vote Eli as Guide. I'll get us across safely.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana's whisper suggests a deal, but I need to see the vote outcome first. No pacts protect me yet. I should vote for someone who might keep me safe or who I can later blame if they fail. Cole's public accountability claim makes him a useful vote—if he wins and lies, he's exposed;
After votes. What do you offer?

events.name: Gus
events.text: I am Gus and want to be Guide myself, so voting for myself secures my chance; a Guide knows the safe panes and I need the survivor advantage. Eli and I have a pact and Eli is my ally, but a self-vote is most useful.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'll be your Guide. Trust the path I call, or lose your footing and your life.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I have a pact with Cole; voting for him keeps it intact and positions us strongly. Others campaigning hard, but loyalty to pact helps jury perception later.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole's my pact partner. Voting him for Guide.
Pact solid. I vote you Guide; save me.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole was elected Guide, which is favorable as I voted for him. I need to position myself favorably on the bridge.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole is Guide, so my pact with him means nothing. I need to maintain safety while keeping options open.
Keep our pact. Vote to swap if we're in danger.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I hold mid-line; no reason to volunteer. Cole as Guide is a risk, but my pacts with Ash and Bex give numbers. Wait and watch.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole is Guide; I have pacts with Bex and Gus. I'm 6th in line, safe for now. Keep quiet and hold.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole won Guide with 3 votes (self, Ash, Hana). I'm 3rd in line with wall approaching. No pacts protecting me. Need to survive round by round, avoid front unless necessary. Swapping back might help but who'd agree? Dara behind me is in Ash-Dara and Bex-Dara pacts - risky to trust.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole is Guide, not me; I'm in the line at position 3 and front is me. Bex's whisper is a manipulation to vote for her; I won't. Holding keeps my pact with Eli intact and avoids the wall; volunteering for the front risks the lead pane. Holding is safest while I watch how Cole call

events.name: Gus
events.text: Holding my place. Watching the Guide's calls before I commit to the front.
Our pact stands. Stay close and watch who the Guide protects.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole is Guide and my pact partner, likely truthful. Stay mid-line for safety. Fenn whisper later, maybe alliance. No swap needed.
Pact offer: vote together, protect each other?

events.name: Ash
events.text: I am Ash, at the front of the line. I need to volunteer to get to the safe platform. It's the best way to survive and get closer to winning.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I volunteer for the front.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash volunteers front, leaving me behind Gus. Gus is unpredictable and my pact with Eli/Gus chain makes me vulnerable to his choices if I move up. Holding keeps my position stable in the middle of the line where risk is shared.
Stay low. Don't swap unless forced. We keep options open.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash volunteered at front, which shields my pact partner. Bex wants a swap only if danger hits. No danger yet; hold and conserve position.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need to stay safe and assess. My pact with Gus is useful, but I must not overcommit. Holding is best this round to see the Guide's calls.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm 4th in line, safe from the wall for now. Hana offered a pact but she's behind me with Cole, and I have no existing pacts. The front is risky - Ash volunteered last round and is now front. I should stay put, observe the Guide's behavior, and not commit yet. Swapping forward is

events.name: Gus
events.text: Round 2, bridge. Front is Ash, who volunteered, and I'm second in line, so I'm not at immediate risk. Eli is my pact partner; keeping it while the front is occupied is cheap. I'll hold and watch the Guide calls before committing.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Still holding. Ash is at the front, so I'll see what the Guide calls before I move.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Bridge needs Guide soon, wall advancing. Cole pacted, but prioritize position. Stay near back, hold for now. Watch others volunteer.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus is at the front after me, and Dara is also a pact partner. Since the goal is to be in the final three, I need to ensure I survive and that those who might vote for me later are also safe. Dara is a pact partner and is behind Gus. I should hold and let Gus take the front. This

events.name: Ash
events.text: I will hold. Let Gus take the front.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Wall advances in three. Eli and Dara are pact partners; keeping both alive secures votes. I must hold to avoid suspicion.
Keep holding. We need three safe at the end.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash volunteered for the front; my pacts with Ash and Bex keep me mid-line. No Guide elected yet—Ash may take it. Hold and stay protected.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash fronted for us. I'd back Ash as Guide—public call, Ash.
Take Guide, call my panes true, and I vote with you to the end.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Keep low and hold. No reason to move or betray yet, but keep options open for later rounds.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm 4th in line with the wall advancing. Ash volunteered front last round and is safe there for now. Gus is behind Ash and seems cautious. I need to avoid being trapped at the back near the wall. Swapping forward could help, but I need a mutual partner. Bex in front of me has mul

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash volunteered for the front and holds the lead; I'm mid-line, not at risk yet. Holding keeps my position and lets the Guide call and the wall reveal before I commit. My pact with Eli stands; no need to break it.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Still holding. Ash is at the front. I'll see what the Guide calls before I move.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash is front, volunteered. Wall advances, need to move forward eventually. Cole pact, but protect myself first. Hold to observe Guide election.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Dara's offer is tempting for jury votes, but I need to assess the risk. If I take Guide, I can ensure my safety and potentially influence others. However, Dara's pacts with Bex and Eli make her a potential threat, and she could still betray me. I will volunteer to be Guide to gai

events.name: Ash
events.text: I will volunteer to be the Guide. Let's see what the path holds.
I'll take Guide. We'll discuss my calls later.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash has publicly declared he will hold, but the line shows him at the front. This is a contradiction that exposes Ash as a potential liar or someone trying to manipulate the vote for Guide. I should not volunteer; my pacts with Eli and Dara are safer if I stay back. I will whispe

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash claims he holds yet stands first. Trust no one blindly until the walk reveals intent.
Ash contradicts himself. Do you still back him?

events.name: Dara
events.text: Wall drops in two rounds; Ash at front with my backing keeps my pacts intact. Staying mid-line is safest. Confirm with Ash, no public promises to others.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Wall drops in two rounds. Ash stays front; I stand by my word.
I backed you publicly. Guide fairly and my pact and vote hold.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash is front and likely safe as Guide? I have pacts with Bex and Gus. Holding is safest; no need to risk yet. Keep Bex and Gus trusting me.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm in the middle of the line (4th of 7), relatively safe. The wall has 2 rounds left. Ash is front and likely to take hits. I should stay put and let others volunteer or get pushed. No need to draw attention. Holding preserves my position and keeps me out of risky swaps.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash has held the front twice and is positioned to be exposed; I want to see the Guide call before committing. Holding keeps my options open and avoids being the one who volunteers into danger.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Still holding. I'll wait for a Guide call before I step forward.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Line is stable, Ash front. Wall has 2 rounds left after this. Hold position, no need to volunteer or swap yet. Guide election soon maybe.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Dara is warning me to guide fairly and threatening to break our pact and vote against me if I don't. I should volunteer to guide to maintain control and potentially secure my position.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I will volunteer to be the Guide again.
I will guide fairly. Your pact and vote are safe.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I am third in line, which is safe for now. Ash is Guide; I should keep my pact with him to ensure his cooperation or at least not provoke an early betrayal. Holding keeps me out of immediate danger while the wall approaches.
Keep us alive. Betrayal now ruins your leverage later.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash as Guide means he's guaranteed safe. I need his true guidance to survive. Bex probes; stay vague. Keep both pacts intact while extracting a commitment from Ash.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Bex, I listen to everyone. Ash, if you Guide, you owe the line honest calls.
Guide me truthfully and my vote follows you to the end. Betray me and Bex

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash is guiding; I need to see if his calls match safe panes. My pact with Bex and Gus is fine, but I hold for now to avoid risk.
Watch Ash's calls closely. I hold unless I see a pattern.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash volunteered as Guide last round and is front. Wall drops in 1 round. I need to survive to final 3. I'm middle position (4th of 7). Swapping back would put me at Eli (last), worst spot. Swapping forward puts me at Bex (3rd) or Gus (2nd) - closer to front, more risk if Guide li
Wall drops next. Hold with me, we move together later.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash is at the front and volunteering; Eli is my pact partner and last in line. Holding keeps my position and avoids exposing my plan. I'll stay put and watch who commits.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Still holding. Let the front walker take the risk first.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Wall advances with 1 round left. Ash volunteered as Guide, now front. Stay back mid-line, hold to survive safely, avoid exposing to lies.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex's whisper is a veiled threat. Dara's whisper is a bribe, likely insincere. Since I am at the front, I must volunteer to ensure my safety and gain information.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'll volunteer to lead us across.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I am safe behind the Guide, Ash. I hold to keep my pact with Eli and Dara intact for now.
Stay quiet. Let Ash call. We move together.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Final round; Ash guides again under our pact. Holding keeps me mid-line with decent odds. No need to rock the boat.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Round six. Ash Guides again. I hold my spot and expect honest calls.
Guide true this round and our pact stands. Lies end it.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need to survive the final round. Ash volunteered as Guide again. My best move is to hold and avoid risk, as the line order puts me last. I have pacts with Bex and Gus; I won't break them now.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding. Trust the Guide's calls enough to stay safe.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Round 6, final round. Ash is front and volunteered to Guide again. The wall has 0 rounds left, so no more wall advancement. I need to survive and reach final three. I'm in position 4 of 7, relatively safe. If I volunteer, I go to front and risk a bad Guide call. Better to hold an

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hold. Let the Guide work.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Round 6 of the bridge; I'm mid-line, Ash is front and volunteered as Guide earlier. Holding keeps me safe from the front risk while others take it. Eli is my pact partner; keep it intact.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Still holding. Front walker takes the first risk again.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Final round, wall advancing. Ash volunteered again, likely to guide/manipulate. Stay safe behind Dara and Fenn, hold position.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Row 1 is R. Hana is my pact partner, so a false call would break the pact and waste a useful shield.

events.name: Cole
events.text: R

events.name: Ash
events.text: Dara's pact hinges on my honesty. Cole, the Guide, called 'R'. I need to decide whether to trust him or counter. Given Dara's warning, a counter might be necessary to maintain the pact. I will counter with 'L' to indicate distrust of Cole's call.
Countering Cole's call to L. Trust me.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole is the Guide and called Right for Ash. I hold pacts with Eli and Dara, so breaking them offers no strategic benefit here. As a non-walker in row 1, waiting avoids unnecessary conflict or signaling my true belief before seeing if Cole's call was honest.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash received the correct call and crossed. No reason to risk my pact with Hana or muddy trust on the first row.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole guides for Hana, not me; his call could be a lie. No information on row one, so counter-calling is a blind gamble. Ash is my pact partner and the walker; I stay quiet and watch.

events.name: Dara
events.text: No proof either way. I hold my call; Ash steps on the Guide's word.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole called R for row 1. I have no info on this row. Waiting avoids risking a false counter-call. Bex and Gus are pacts but I don't need to act here.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole called R for Ash on row 1. I have no private info about Cole's honesty. Counter-calling risks nothing for me personally since I'm not the walker, but needlessly antagonizing the Guide early could backfire. Better to wait, observe patterns, and let others test Cole's reliabil

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole called R for row 1 and Ash is walking. Guide may lie; no evidence yet. Countering costs nothing but exposes me as a contrarian. Waiting keeps me flexible and avoids a false-call trap.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Waiting on Cole's call. No counter yet.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole called R for Ash on row 1. We're pact-bound. Countering L accuses him of lying, risks breaking pact early. Wait to see.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole is the guide and knows the safe path. Ash is the front walker. Cole has not made a call yet. The previous counter-call from Ash was to step L. Given this, Ash should step L.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I step left.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I am a juror now. I need to give my last words to the camera and make sure they are memorable, as they will be seen by the remaining contestants and the jury.

events.name: Ash
events.text: A tough loss, but I'll be watching. The jury will decide the ultimate winner. Play smart.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Row 2 is safely L. Hana is my pact partner, so a truthful call preserves the pact and avoids needless jury damage.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Call left. The row-two safe pane is L.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole is my rival and guide; his call for Gus to go Left could be a trap or genuine. Since I have no private information, waiting is the safest move to let others commit first.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Row two is L. Reinforcing my accurate call protects Hana pact optics while advancing Gus and preserving leverage.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Counter left. Row two is L.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole guided Ash left and Ash died on row 1's weak L pane. Cole already lied once, so his row-2 call of L is suspect. I'll counter right.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole's last call killed Ash. His L call is worthless. I counter right.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole is guide and called L. Row 1 was weak L, so row 2 is independent; no pattern. I have no reason to counter if I trust Cole, but he might lie. I'll wait to avoid drawing attention or breaking pacts.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole is Guide and called L for row 2. Gus is the walker. I have no reason to trust Cole—he has a pact with Hana and no loyalty to me. Countering risks nothing for me personally since I'm not walking, but could build trust with Gus or damage Cole's credibility. However, making ene

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole called L publicly for row 2; Cole is a rival and may lie. Row 1's weak pane was L, which says nothing about row 2. Waiting keeps me unexposed while I weigh whether Cole benefits from sending me left. Breaking my pact with Eli now gains nothing yet.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole called L for row 2. Ash died on row 1 L, which was weak. No pattern confirmed. Trust pact partner Cole for now; wait to see counters.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Row 2 call from Guide Cole is L, but Dara counter-called R and Cole's prior call killed Ash, so Cole is suspect. Rows are independent, so row 1's weak L says nothing about row 2. With two conflicting calls and a liar possible, I lean R, the side Dara claims and which opposes the

events.name: Gus
events.text: I am eliminated and now a juror; I should give brief last words. Revealing the weak pane helps those still crossing, and it's a neutral public fact that may matter to jury impressions.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Right side of row two is weak. Don't trust it. Good luck, survivors.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Row 3 is L. Bex is not my pact partner, so truthful guidance preserves leverage without breaking Hana pact.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Call left. Row three is L.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole has called L for Bex. My revealed weak pane for row 2 was R, meaning L was safe there, but past rows don't guarantee future ones. Cole lied previously (Ash died on his call), so I must distrust him. If I counter R, and it's wrong, I die. If I wait, I follow Cole's L. Given A

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole lied before. He's trying to drop me. I'm taking the other side.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Row 3 is L. Reinforcing my accurate call protects Bex and preserves Hana pact without revealing more information.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Left is safe; follow the Guide call.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole's L call was right for row two; my counter:R killed Gus and looks terrible to the jury. I stay silent this row and let Cole take responsibility.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole's past L call led to death; but counter-calling L could save Bex if true, while Dara's R call might be manipulative. Yet Cole's record is bad. Since Bex and I have a pact, I should protect her by countering what I believe. Weak panes: row1 L, row2 R, so no pattern. I'll coun

events.name: Eli
events.text: Counter left to keep Bex safe.
I believe left; Dara may be lying.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole's L call killed Ash on row 1, but row 2's weak was R so his L call was actually correct there—Gus died because Dara's counter was wrong. Cole has been right twice. Dara has pacts with Ash (dead) and Bex; she may be trying to undermine Cole to break Bex-Eli or build her own c

events.name: Hana
